system: You are an expert in machine-learning research who organises research ideas into method families.
user:
Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

Below are 24 candidate research ideas for this problem. Group them into 4-7 method families such that ideas in the same family share their core mechanism (not merely their goal). Give each family a short name.

[B1-g0-C1] Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive per-image MVFA scoring
Replace test-set min-max normalisation with each branch's leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores, fuse in CDF space, and pool with a top-k mean.

[B1-g0-C2] Source-episode Platt calibration with support re-centring for per-image MVFA scores
Learn per-branch logistic calibration and fusion weights on simulated few-shot episodes from the source modalities, then re-centre them on the target with the K support normals only.

[B1-g0-C3] Two-anchor scaling with support normals and synthetic lesions for inductive MVFA scoring
Normalise each MVFA branch between the median score of the support normals and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into those supports, so no test-set statistics are needed.

[B1-g0-C4] Prototype-radius normalisation of MVFA's few-shot branch for per-image scoring
Cluster the support patch features into normal prototypes per level, score test patches by distance to the nearest prototype divided by its radius, and fuse with a support-standardised zero-shot branch.

[B1-g0-C5] Log-odds fusion of temperature-calibrated MVFA branches for inductive scoring
Calibrate the zero-shot branch with a source-fitted temperature, map the few-shot branch to a probability with support statistics, and add the two log-odds instead of min-max normalising and averaging.

[B1-g0-C6] Region-mass aggregation with support-derived thresholds for robust per-image MVFA scores
Standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, threshold the fused map at a support-derived level, and score each image by the excess mass of its strongest connected region.

[B1-g1-o1] Target-local Platt scaling from support normals and synthetic lesions, fused in log-odds
Fit the few-shot branch's logistic calibration on the target itself, using leave-one-out support normals as negatives and synthetic lesions pasted into the supports as positives, keep a source-fitted temperature for the zero-shot branch, and add the two log-odds.

[B1-g1-o2] Conformal few-shot p-values and temperature-calibrated zero-shot probabilities fused in log-odds
Turn the few-shot branch into a conformal p-value from the leave-one-out support distribution, keep the zero-shot branch as a temperature-calibrated probability, and combine both in log-odds with weights fitted on source episodes.

[B1-g1-o3] Support-CDF scores with source-episode isotonic calibration of the fused score
Map both branches through their leave-one-out support CDFs, average them, and convert the fused CDF score into a probability with an isotonic map learned on source-modality episodes.

[B1-g1-o4] Binomial exceedance test: per-image p-values from support-calibrated pixel thresholds
Set a pixel threshold so that a known small fraction of support-normal pixels exceed it, and score each test image by the binomial tail probability of its observed number of exceeding pixels.

[B1-g1-o5] Upper-tail Wasserstein score: comparing each image's patch-score distribution with the support-normal distribution
Score each test image by the 1-Wasserstein distance between the upper tail of its own patch-score distribution and the upper tail of the pooled leave-one-out support-normal patch scores, giving a per-image score that needs no test-set statistics and is insensitive to single pixels.

[B1-g1-o6] Scan statistic over calibrated log-odds maps with a support-derived null for the image score
Score each image by the largest summed log-odds over connected candidate regions of its calibrated anomaly map, and convert it to a p-value with the null distribution of that maximum built from leave-one-out support normals.

[B1-g2-o1] Level-wise conformal p-values combined with the Cauchy rule and calibrated isotonically
Compute a conformal p-value for each MVFA feature level and branch from leave-one-out support scores, combine the eight dependent p-values with the Cauchy combination test, and map the result to a probability with a source-fitted isotonic map.

[B1-g2-o2] Augmentation-consistency scoring: true anomalies persist under flips and small shifts, spurious responses do not
Score each test image under eight label-preserving augmentations (flips and half-patch shifts), and use a conformal p-value of the augmentation-averaged score together with its across-augmentation spread to down-weight unstable responses.

[B1-g2-o3] Weighted conformal scoring that borrows source-modality normals to stabilise small support sets
Enlarge the leave-one-out reference set of the few-shot branch at small K by adding normal source-modality images, weighted by their feature similarity to the target supports (weighted conformal prediction), so per-image p-values remain fine-grained and valid under modality shift.

[B1-g2-o4] Extreme-value (peaks-over-threshold) calibration of per-image MVFA scores
Fit a generalised Pareto distribution to the upper tail of leave-one-out support-normal patch scores and score each test image by the tail probability of its highest patch scores, which extrapolates beyond the few observed support values.

[B1-g2-o5] Selective per-image MVFA scoring with a conformal abstention band
Give each image one of three outputs, normal, abnormal or refer to a reader, by placing an abstention band on its conformal p-value, and measure the risk-coverage trade-off that a deployable MVFA would offer.

[B1-g2-o6] Weight-free fusion of MVFA branches by a Bonferroni-corrected minimum p-value
Replace inverse-variance fusion weights with a weight-free rule: convert each branch to a support-based conformal p-value and score the image by twice the smaller of the two, which is valid whatever the dependence between branches.

[B1-g3-o1] Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of support statistics for stable per-image MVFA scores at small K
Stabilise the support-derived normalisation statistics used for per-image scoring by shrinking each branch's support mean and spread toward priors learned across source modalities, with the amount of shrinkage set by K, as in small-area estimation.

[B1-g3-o2] Subjective-logic fusion of MVFA branches with an explicit uncertainty mass from support size
Express each branch's per-image evidence as a subjective-logic opinion (belief in abnormal, belief in normal, uncertainty) whose uncertainty mass shrinks as K grows, fuse the two opinions with the cumulative fusion operator, and score images by projected probability while reporting uncertainty.

[B1-g3-o3] Joint score-space density of support normals for fusing MVFA's two branches
Instead of fusing the zero-shot and few-shot scores by a fixed rule, model the joint distribution of the two branch scores on leave-one-out support normals (plus source normals for stability) and score each image by its negative log-density, so the fusion follows the actual correlation between branches.

[B1-g3-o4] Online false-discovery-rate control over a stream of MVFA-scored images
Treat deployment as a stream of incoming images, each with a per-image conformal p-value from MVFA, and flag images with an online FDR procedure (LORD) so that the proportion of false alarms among flagged images stays below a target over time, without ever using batch statistics.

[B1-g3-o5] Cauchy-combined level-wise conformal few-shot evidence fused in log-odds with a temperature-calibrated zero-shot branch
Replace the single fused few-shot conformal p-value with a Cauchy combination of the four level-wise conformal p-values, then fuse it with the temperature-calibrated zero-shot probability in log-odds as in the conformal parent.

[B1-g3-o6] Random-effects meta-analysis across MVFA levels and branches for per-image scores
Treat each of MVFA's level-branch maps as a separate study estimating how abnormal an image is, with its own support-derived standard error, and pool them with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model so that inconsistent levels are down-weighted for that image.
